summary_rationale: Lowe's Companies, Inc. is the entrenched number-two franchise in a structurally protected U.S. home improvement duopoly, operating 1,762 retail stores (approximately 89% owned, including stores on leased land) alongside over 540 newly acquired Pro branches and 120 supply chain facilities. Even during a multi-year trough in U.S. existing-home turnover, Lowe's generated $86,286 million in FY2025 net sales, a 33.48% gross margin, $10,153 million in GAAP operating income (11.77% margin), 26.1% return on invested capital, $9,864 million in operating cash flow, and $7,651 million in free cash flow (115.0% conversion of GAAP net earnings). That cash engine supports more than 50 consecutive years of dividend increases. However, KPI health warrants a PASS_WITH_WATCH designation for four forensic reasons. First, retail customer transactions declined for three consecutive fiscal years (827 million in FY2023 to 780 million in FY2025) and fell another 1.7% in Q3 FY2026, leaving positive comparable sales (+1.8% in Q3 FY2026) reliant on ticket inflation and online growth (+17.4%). Second, consolidated GAAP operating margin compressed from 13.38% in FY2023 to 11.77% in FY2025 and is guided to 11.1% (11.5% adjusted) in FY2026 due to wage deleverage on flat retail comps and margin dilution from wholesale Pro acquisitions. Third, the $10.1 billion cash acquisitions of Artisan Design Group ($1.3 billion, June 2025) and Foundation Building Materials ($8.8 billion, October 2025) added $9.4 billion of goodwill and intangibles, lifted total debt to $37.55 billion plus $4.47 billion of operating leases as of October 30, 2026, and forced a share-repurchase pause until leverage returns to 2.75x adjusted debt-to-EBITDAR by mid-2027. Fourth, Q3 FY2026 earnings included a $250 million ($0.34 per share) IEEPA tariff refund that temporarily cushioned diesel and mix headwinds.
